discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 9338bc95a5. When a provider has no key and no URL, `providerResolver` now asks core's `isProviderSettingsUsable` (the check the CLI and desktop provider pickers use) instead of refusing outright, so Bedrock through a profile, IAM, access keys or the default credential chain (region and bearer token may come from the environment), Vertex with GCP credentials and local sign-ins like claude-code reach the planner. Entries with a key or URL resolve as before.

Addressed in the follow-up commit: the new `charges a flat ESTIMATED_TOKENS_PER_IMAGE per image` test asserts the delta for one image is `ESTIMATED_TOKENS_PER_IMAGE` plus the JSON overhead and that payload length leaves the estimate unchanged, with the same payload-length check added to the `createTokenEstimator` test. Removing the per-image term now fails the suite.

Addressed in `a138a042d`. I now snapshot the active turn model-dependent state and defer provider/model selection changes to the next fully rebuilt run; in-place refresh remains limited to the current selection. The added Core regressions cover tool-capable to image-model and provider changes while preserving the current turn tools, completion policy, `prepareTurn`, and result metadata.

vLLM's `/v1/models` reports the window as `max_model_len` (it's on its ModelCard), so a vLLM source still falls back to 128K even though the comment at the top lists vLLM. Worth adding `entry.max_model_len` here?

On LM Studio's `/api/v0/models`, `max_context_length` is the model's ceiling, and a loaded model also reports `loaded_context_length`, which is what it actually serves (can be a lot smaller). Since maxInputTokens falls back to contextWindow and that's the compaction budget, compaction won't kick in before LM Studio starts rejecting. Prefer `loaded_context_length` when it's present?

Fixed in 2c1a7f7d7: normalization now recurses into `items` (object and tuple forms) and into `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf` branches before the object-likeness gate, so nested uppercase types lowercase at every depth. Covered by the new "normalizes nested array items and combinator branches" test.
is this pattern present elsewhere in the codebase? seems like special handling for bedrock which I'd like to avoid if possible
what do you think about making a pr upstream to the ai-sdk itself to fix the bedrock adapter so that it doesn't accidentally send reasoning. seems like the better place for the fix to live

discussion_comments.comment_body: Correct, and thanks for the precision. Registering the model only takes model *selection* off the catalog; `resolveBedrockModelId` still consults it, and with #14480 on main the bare `openai.gpt-6-astra` case goes out as `us.openai.gpt-6-astra` in us-east-1. Comment and PR description narrowed accordingly.
